attributes.action: Aerial Support needs to be provided to tackle the Rhinogydd wildfires NOW
attributes.additional_details: Firefighters need aerial support to put out a fire that has been ravaging habitats and land for 9 days. It allegedly started by a visitor wildcamping when using a stove in the heatwave. No aerial support has been arranged by authorities, and RAF Valley allegedly cannot provide support even though this fire is in the route they use for training purposes. NRW said they had aerial support planned for the 20th July, but that has not materialised and NRW allegedly will not procure a private aircraft.
attributes.background: We are now into Day 9 of the fires on the Rhinogydd area in North West Wales which includes area of rare and protected habitats, which also had rare protected species. This fire is spreading, threatening to devastate property, infrastructure, further habitats and species, aswell as impacting health.

rejection.details:
Your petition is about something that the Welsh Government and Welsh Parliament is responsible for. That means that the UK Government and Parliament can't look into it.

The Welsh Parliament has its own Petitions Committee. If you'd like to send your petition to the Welsh Parliament, you can find out more here: https://petitions.senedd.wales/

You may also wish to raise this issue with your local Members of the Senedd who represents you. You can find out who your Members of the Senedd are and how to contact them here: https://senedd.wales/find-a-member-of-the-senedd/
